Cluster B Personality Disorders

borderline · antisocial · histrionic · narcissisticA lifelong pattern, or an episode of mood or psychosis?

1Script2Urgent3Differential4Workup5Criteria6Severity7Treatment8Follow-upPractice
1Illness script
Bottom line
  • A lifelong pattern, present by early adulthood and generally stable across settings; instability that comes in episodes with a start and an end points to a mood disorder
  • Borderline: abandonment fear, unstable relationships and self-image, self-harm, and transient stress-related paranoia lasting minutes to hours; first-line treatment is psychotherapy, with the best evidence for dialectical behavior therapy
  • Antisocial needs age 18 or older and conduct disorder before 15; under 18, antisocial personality disorder cannot be diagnosed; consider conduct disorder
What it is

Cluster B: the dramatic, emotional or erratic personality disorders: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic The three clustersCluster A weird, cluster B wild, cluster C worried

Driver

Rigid, pervasive patterns of thinking, feeling and relating distress or impaired function

Triggers

Conduct disorder in childhood (antisocial)

Childhood trauma: abuse or neglect (borderline)

Mood and substance use disorders in the family non-modifiable

Chain

Development: childhood trauma or insecure attachment fear of abandonment

Pattern: splitting, people seen as all good or all bad unstable, intense relationships

Crisis: a stressor such as a breakup self-injury, suicidal threats, or paranoia and dissociation for minutes to hours

Insights

Psychosis here is brief and tied to stress; persistent delusions more likely mean a primary psychotic disorder

Borderline mood shifts moment to moment, often with stressors, and never reaches a sustained manic or hypomanic episode

Comorbidity and coursetap to open
ComorbidCommon: screen for and treat these disordersMood and substance use disorders often coexist with cluster B
BorderlineDissociation, such as depersonalization, is common after traumaAbout 10% die by suicide; most remit with treatment
AntisocialMore common in menSome behaviors may lessen around age 40 to 50
Borderline and sexDiagnosed more often in women
2Urgent risks
SuicideSuicidal threats, gestures or attempts, and often nonsuicidal self-injury such as cutting

If there is suicidal talk or self-harm, choose assess suicide risk.

3Differential
Look-alikes, most tempting first
DiagnosisFingerprintDecides it
Impulsive, unstable, seductive or recklessMania 1 week or more, hypomania 4 days or more: episodes with a start and an end; personality traits are lifelong and pervasive
Paranoia or voices after a stressor1 day to under 1 month; transient stress-related paranoia in borderline personality disorder passes within minutes to hours
Low mood, suicidal thoughts2 weeks or more of sustained symptoms; loss of mood reactivity marks melancholic depression, while borderline mood reacts to each stressor
Lying, truancy, theft, fightingUnder 18: antisocial personality disorder needs age 18 or older and conduct disorder before 15
Odd or eccentric; detached or suspiciousLifelong oddness, not drama or instability
4Workup
Clues that change the answer
CluePoints toNext move
Staff split into all good and all badBorderline personality disorderDiagnose it; treat as in step 7
Paranoia or detachment for hours after a breakupTransient stress-related paranoia of borderline personality disorderDiagnose borderline personality disorder; treat as in step 7
Seductive, theatrical and attention seeking for yearsHistrionic personality disorderDiagnose it; screen for comorbid disorders as in Next step
Grandiose, entitled, enraged by criticismNarcissistic personality disorderDiagnose it; treat as in step 7
Fraud, fights and no remorse in an adult with childhood conduct problemsAntisocial personality disorderDiagnose it; screen for substance use as in Next step
Seductive and grandiose for days, with little sleep and rapid speechA manic episode

Pause point. The bait: bipolar disorder for borderline mood swings, or brief psychotic disorder for stress paranoia. Lifelong, reactive instability with psychosis lasting hours is borderline personality disorder.

5Diagnostic criteria
Defining criteria: Cluster B All – present by early adulthood, generally stable across settings · Antisocial – unlawful acts, deceit, impulsivity, aggression, no remorse; age 18 or older with conduct disorder before 15 · Borderline – 5 or more of the features below · Histrionic – shifting, exaggerated emotion; attention seeking; sexually provocative · Narcissistic – grandiosity, entitlement, need for admiration, exploits others, lacks empathy
Borderline: the 9 features, by area
AreaFeature
RelationshipsFrantic efforts to avoid abandonment; unstable, intense relationships
SelfUnstable self-image; chronic emptiness
BehaviorSelf-damaging impulsivity in 2 or more areas; recurrent suicidal behavior or self-injury
MoodMarked mood reactivity; intense, inappropriate anger
Under stressTransient paranoia or dissociation
7Treatment
1

First lineBorderline

Psychotherapy: dialectical behavior therapy has the best evidence; transference-focused psychotherapy also works
2

AdjunctSevere mood instability or transient paranoia

A mood stabilizer, or a second-generation antipsychotic
3

Comorbid disorderDepression or anxiety

An antidepressant for that disorder, not for the personality disorder
First treatment by situation
SituationChooseWatch for
BorderlineDialectical behavior therapy; the team sees the patient jointlySplitting of staff into good and bad
AntisocialTreat comorbid substance use and mood disorders; psychotherapy has not proven effectiveSome behaviors may lessen around 40 to 50
HistrionicTreat comorbid somatic symptom, conversion or depressive disorders; psychotherapy helps littleMay improve with engagement in therapy
NarcissisticPsychotherapy: psychodynamic, transference-focused or dialectical behavior therapyAggression predicts a worse course
8Follow-up
Follow-up decisions
WhenDo or expect
Borderline, over timeExpect sustained remission with treatment in most; about 10% die by suicide
Antisocial, in middle ageSome behaviors may lessen; the course stays chronic
Practice
  1. 26-year-old woman, mood shifts within hours after arguments with her partner cuts her forearms when he threatens to leave; feels empty idealizes, then despises, each new friend no week-long periods of elevated mood or reduced need for sleep → Borderline personality disorder → reactive mood shifts within hours, abandonment fear, self-injury, emptiness and splitting, with no sustained hypomanic episode: borderline personality disorder; bipolar disorder needs sustained manic or hypomanic episodes
  2. 22-year-old man arrested for selling fake concert tickets online expelled at 14 for stealing and fighting; set fires as a child laughs off the victims' losses; several bar fights this year mood euthymic · no psychotic symptoms → Antisocial personality disorder → an adult with fraud, aggression and no remorse, and conduct problems before 15: antisocial personality disorder; antisocial personality disorder cannot be diagnosed under 18, and narcissism centers on grandiosity rather than lawbreaking
  3. 16-year-old boy brought in by his father after a third school suspension steals from classmates, starts fights, skips school for days once hurt the neighbor's dog; lies about where he goes behavior began around age 11 → Conduct disorder → repeated theft, fighting, cruelty and truancy under age 18: conduct disorder; antisocial personality disorder needs age 18 or older, and oppositional defiant disorder lacks aggression, cruelty and property violations
  4. 24-year-old woman with borderline personality disorder seen after another cutting episode wounds superficial; no suicidal plan or intent today relationships stormy; mood swings within hours no depressive episode; no persistent psychosis → Dialectical behavior therapy → psychotherapy is the primary treatment for borderline personality disorder, with the best evidence for dialectical behavior therapy; medication is only an adjunct, for example for severe mood instability or transient paranoia
  5. 31-year-old woman whose coworkers call her "always on stage" dresses provocatively; flirts with the physician; cries, then laughs pattern since her late teens sleeps 8 hours; speech normal in rate; no recent change in energy → Histrionic personality disorder → years of theatrical, shifting emotion, seductiveness and attention seeking with normal sleep and speech: histrionic personality disorder; mania is an episode with less need for sleep and rapid speech, and narcissism seeks admiration through grandiosity
  6. 27-year-old woman brought in after threatening to overdose when her boyfriend left recalls feeling outside her own body that night scars from cutting; years of stormy relationships sleep, appetite and energy unchanged → Childhood abuse or neglect → borderline personality disorder, with suicidal threats on abandonment, self-injury and stress dissociation; a history of childhood trauma is often found, while manic episodes are not part of the picture
Pairs with Hears Voices or Holds Odd Beliefs: cluster A and transient stress-related paranoia of borderline personality disorder among the psychotic look-alikes. Bipolar Disorder: a manic or hypomanic episode. Suicide Risk Assessment: self-harm and suicidal threats. Disruptive Behavior in a Child: conduct disorder before 18.
Transferable rule

Personality disorders are lifelong and pervasive: before naming one, make sure the instability is not an episode of mania or depression, and that any psychosis lasted only minutes to hours.
